stage_a.note: Smiling broadly and delivering with upbeat energy while discussing the yogurt category analogy.
Emphatic delivery and gestures when stating 'I am a grown woman, I am not doing pouches'.
Friendly, smiling, and making good eye contact while offering samples to the panel.

venture.description: Gourmet, adult-focused applesauce with exotic flavors and apple wedges, packaged in glass jars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 delivers the prepared pitch, introducing her adult-focused applesauce and asking for $150K for 15 percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 transitions to handing out samples of the different flavors to the panel.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 eagerly accepts the sample.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 expresses his love for applesauce.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 notes that they are tasting four of the six available flavors.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 thanks F1 for the sample.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 thanks F1 as she hands him his sample.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 asks S3 if the guava flavor is good.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 confirms she likes the guava flavor.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 adds that the plain apple flavor is delicious.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 points out that the plain apple is the unsweetened version.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 remarks that it does not taste processed.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if the product is currently available in the market or if it is brand new.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains they launched a direct-to-consumer test market for six months starting in July.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what their sales figures are today.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states they achieved $40,000 in sales during their six-month test pilot.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if customers are buying it for the flavor or as a health food.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains customers buy it because they want plant-based options, are moving away from dairy, or want to bake vegan.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks how she sells the product and what the cost is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states the glass jars will be on Amazon Prime in a 4-pack, costing $1.03 to make and $3.99 retail.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 calculates that a 4-pack retails for $16 with a cost of $4.12 and asks to confirm.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms S1's calculation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 challenges the price, asking if it is not expensive for applesauce.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 defends the price using the Chobani analogy and claims they recently generated $35M in projected revenue at a trade show.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 explicitly rejects her $35M revenue claim, saying he is not buying it.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks F1 to explain how they reached that $35M figure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains that buyers from major retailers like Starbucks and Whole Foods were sending other buyers to their booth.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 clarifies if these buyers were actually giving her orders.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits it wasn't an order-taking conference but notes they already had a commitment with Whole Foods beforehand.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks if the Whole Foods commitment is just a test.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms it is a test in one Whole Foods store in Harlem.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 pushes back, asking how she got to the $35M figure if she only has one test store.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 attempts to explain the figure by referring to the number of buyers who approached them.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks directly if they received a firm order from anybody.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits they have no firm orders, only confirmed interest from buyers who see the product as unique.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 observes that the new product format is a yogurt cup rather than a glass jar.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 notes the difference and asks to see the new cup format.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 hands out the plastic cups, explaining this is the product they are pitching to grocers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 remarks that the plastic cup format is a better idea.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 verifies if the cups contain the same flavors.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks F1 about her professional background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 details her role as Global Head of HR for News Corp and her experience building high-performance teams.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 challenges her, asking if she is not going to work full-time on the venture.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 admits it doesn't make sense for her to be full-time yet, but notes her COO is full-time.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks if she has raised a lot of money, noting the operation sounds expensive.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains she has self-funded the business so far, spending $250,000 of her own money.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 compliments F1, stating she has gotten very far for the amount she spent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks about her plan for balancing the glass jar product versus the plastic cup product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states that the glass jars will launch on Amazon Prime in two weeks.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 challenges the Amazon launch, arguing that the shipping cost for glass jars will be enormous.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 defends the glass format by stating they are still able to make 46 percent margins on it.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 asks what the cost of the plastic cup version will be.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains the plastic cup costs 63 cents to make, wholesales for around a dollar, and retails for $1.79.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 challenges her pricing again, declaring it the most expensive applesauce ever sold in America.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 replies that traditional applesauce buyers are not their target consumer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 argues that creating a new category in glass will be nearly impossible and asks why she complicates the model.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 briefly acknowledges his point, stating that the glass format is simply where they started.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 explains she is not a fan of applesauce and doubts its popularity among adults, leading to her exit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 accepts S2's decision and respects her perspective.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 expresses disappointment, stating the presentation was impressive until she mentioned the trade show.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 declares he is out because she confused trade show interest with actual orders, creating doubt.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 politely accepts S4's decision to exit.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 praises the product's flavor and format, and notes she does not think the price is out of line.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 expresses skepticism about the valuation and asks if any offer would insult F1 at this point.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 replies that no offer would insult her and is curious to hear S3's valuation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 offers the requested $150,000 but demands 75 percent equity in return.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 restates her offer of $150,000 for 75 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 asks F1 if S3's offer insulted her.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 responds that the offer did not insult her, but found it interesting.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 asks F1 directly if she would like to accept the offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 rejects S3's offer, stating it is not one they can take.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: S3 immediately exits following the rejection.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 challenges F1's commitment, stating she should quit her job and work full-time if she truly believes in it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains she works weekends but is also the breadwinner, making quitting not an option for everyone.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 shows understanding, agreeing that not everyone can afford to quit their job.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 declares he can only invest in entrepreneurs who are full-time and exits the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 asks F1 how much cash she currently has in the bank for the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 states she has set aside close to $500,000 for the business since she is self-funding.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 clarifies if she has already put in $250,000 and has another $250,000 in savings.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 confirms S1's understanding of her financial commitment.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 challenges her entrepreneurial drive, arguing that she didn't have to start the business and isn't fully committed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 insists she works around the clock and that it is definitely not a casual part-time gig.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: S5 interrupts to emphasize that she still works somewhere else.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 acknowledges her other job but argues she has put a dedicated team in place to compensate.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 continues to press her, asking why she isn't throwing everything into the business.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: S4 defends F1, arguing that not everyone has the luxury to quit their job due to family responsibilities.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 notices F1's emotion and asks her to explain why she is tearing up.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 explains she is the breadwinner for her family and would not risk their security if she didn't believe.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 asks F1 specifically who relies on her financially.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 lists her parents and siblings, noting she is the one who made it financially.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: S2 validates F1's choice, agreeing she is right to keep her job and take care of her family.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 expresses his belief in her and offers $150,000 for 25 percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: F1 accepts S1's offer, stating she is comfortable doing that.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: S1 confirms the deal and moves to hug F1.

exchanges.label: Kevin challenging lack of full-time commitment
Cash invested and Mark challenging commitment
Founder's emotional response and family reliance

decisions.note: Not an applesauce fan, doesn't believe in the product for herself.
Uncomfortable with founder confusing trade show interest with actual orders.
Believes in the product but feels the valuation is too high and it's a risky dream.
Offer takes too much equity, not something she can accept.
Cannot invest in an entrepreneur who does not work on the business full-time.
Impressed by the founder and believes his team can help with the missing pieces.
Comfortable giving up 25% for Mark's help.
